Replay

Aim and historical queries

4 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Collision storagePresentation and spawn identity

Model.step_view is the simulation callback for games that need the view associated with each control sample. It replaces Model.step for that model; existing models can keep step. Both execute the same complete-world prediction/correction loop.

Draw remote players with client_present(&client). It returns two authoritative frames and a quantized interpolation fraction and remembers their snapshot IDs. Compute aim from those same drawn positions. Subsequent client_step calls bind that bracket to their controls; receiving a newer snapshot does not rewrite the earlier aiming context. Calling client_observed alone does not bind a context.

Presentation drift is bounded by watch_delay + view_slack behind the latest installed authority frame. After a sparse delivery or local stall, the observed clock catches up to that bound. If the available interpolation endpoints exceed max_view_span, it advances to the newer received endpoint. Stats.watch_catchups counts these advances. Watched events advance with that same clock. This may skip an old visual interval; it prevents lingering on views whose proofs have expired. Previously captured aiming stamps stay unchanged, and the server still validates their identity and age. Catch-up does not turn rejected history into a live query.

The server resolves the transmitted View_Stamp into a View_Time:

  • Historical: both snapshot IDs/ticks were sent to this connection in its current generation/checkpoint serial, the bracket is bounded, and its age at receipt is within policy.
  • Live: authority-local input, querying the current simulation step.
  • Unavailable: no observed view was supplied.
  • Invalid: malformed bracket or unknown/mismatched snapshot identity.
  • Expired: a known view exceeds the allowed age. A previously accepted view can also expire before its scheduled simulation tick executes.

Only control ownership and ordinary input validity determine whether movement is accepted. An invalid view disables that input's historical query; it does not discard otherwise valid movement. Reliable actions remain a separate API.

Defaults allow 30 ticks of rewind, a 12-tick interpolation span and four ticks of timing slack. At receipt, the age bound is the smaller of max_rewind and the measured snapshot-ack RTT floor in ticks plus watch_delay + view_slack. Until an RTT observation exists, the absolute bound applies. A two-second measurement window lets the floor adapt to route changes. Execution applies max_rewind again so queued or held inputs cannot keep a historical query alive indefinitely. These settings, including watch delay, participate in the connection contract.

These are bounded, validated hints, not proof of what a physical display showed. A client can select another known bracket within policy or delay acknowledgements; the absolute cap still applies. Competitive deployments must choose suitable caps and trust only their authority's world/collision data.

Collision storage#

replay/history.History(T, N) is a value-owned ring. Put it in World when its contents influence simulation. It then participates in correction, canonical snapshots, saves and migration. read/bracket return copies and explicit misses; they never temporarily move live entities. This initial representation trades copying/bandwidth for a straightforward complete-world contract.

query_view(&history, view, live, tick, blend) resolves the validated View_Time against that ring and returns {value, status, tick, available}. Live requests use the supplied current value. Historical requests require both retained endpoints; missing history becomes Unavailable, malformed ranges become Invalid, and rejected view statuses stay unavailable. There is no live fallback. Read value only when available is true. The helper does not authenticate raw client stamps; the runner does that before supplying View_Time to step_view.

The game supplies a pure blend(a, b, fraction) for its collision snapshot and checks the resulting lifetime IDs against current entities before applying effects. Quickdraw and Scrapyard use this helper with different proxy representations. History values, including generation changes, remain part of rollback/checkpoints.

Quickdraw records four replay/play.Hurtbox2 proxies after movement each tick. Its ray starts at the live shooter's position, queries the validated historical target bracket, and clips against authored static walls/crates. A life identifier prevents an old body from hitting a respawned player. Missing history or rejected view context produces an explicit miss. The A/B control intentionally queries live targets instead. A game chooses its own policy; there is no hidden fallback to current collision poses.

Validated held/future view contexts are archived alongside controls. Network snapshot proofs are connection-local and rebuilt on rejoin. As with existing control streams, reconnect retires archived remote inputs and samples a fresh stream; archived reliable action IDs follow the selected recovery policy.

Presentation and spawn identity#

Supply Model.event_owner and call client_remote_observed to present local effects speculatively and remote effects on the observed clock. The journal still delivers Begin/Update/Cancel/Confirm. Clients that do not opt in retain their existing policy. Keep the client at a stable address: the policy carries a borrowed pointer to that client.

Godot Session/Room callers can set Session_Options.remote_observed=true instead of reinstalling the policy after role changes. Quickdraw clears scene instances on epoch/Welcome reset and scopes active beam cancellation to the full event ID, so cancellation of an old shot cannot erase a newer shot's beam.

Quickdraw predicts the complete world but draws remote bodies/projectiles from observed frames. This is mixed presentation, not a partial-world predictor or an owner-authoritative physics mode. Owner observations and prediction groups have separate contracts.

replay/play.spawn_key(tick, seat, ordinal) supplies a bounded semantic ID for predicted view lifetime. Authority and prediction can allocate different pool slots and still identify the same projectile. Pool generations continue to govern simulation handles. An application must reset its view namespace on authority epoch changes; the spawn key alone is not an epoch-qualified global ID.

Gameplay protocol is version 7; complete authority archives are version 4. Earlier experimental packets/archives are rejected. Authority control RPC and coordinator decision record versions are independent.
